title: footgun: TransactionResult.clampedPayload reads as 'the payload that will be applied', implying it is meaningful only on success and empty otherwise.
detail: On the failure paths at lines 82-87 (source has no state) and 100-105 (source entry invalid), the returned object has success:false but clampedPayload set to the capacity-clamped payload (non-empty), while the other two failures return {}. A caller that applies clampedPayload without checking success would move resources on a failed transaction; the field's population is inconsistent across failure branches.

title: footgun: status is typed 'completed' | 'extinction' and readStateValue/isExtinct suggest any tick where population<=0 ends the run as extinction.
detail: status only becomes 'extinction' (and the loop breaks) when isExtinct && i > 10 (line 93). If population reaches 0 at loop index <= 10 it is snapshotted but the run continues and, if population stays 0, still returns status:'completed'. Early extinction is silently reported as a completed run.

title: footgun: The variable is named blueprintSettings, implying it holds blueprint-level settings.
detail: It is read from cartridge.config?.settings, and the if/else makes config.settings and assets.settings mutually exclusive: when config.settings is present, cartridge.assets?.settings is never walked, so any asset-defined setting levers are silently omitted whenever config settings also exist.

title: footgun: InstantTransferHandler is registered like any typed handler via runtime.registerCommandHandler.
detail: It is force-cast through `as unknown as CommandHandler<RuntimeCommand>` (it only implements CommandHandler<TransferAssetsCommand>), defeating the compiler check, and registerHandler stores handlers in a Map keyed by handler.type, so this registration silently overwrites any previously-registered TRANSFER_ASSETS handler rather than adding to it.

title: InstantTransferHandler reimplements creditResources instead of reusing the shared one
detail: creditResources and ensureStateRecord here duplicate the semantics of transferResources.ts creditResources (lines 93-125), which the file already imports debitResources from. The two copies have already drifted (error strings 'Transfer failed:' vs 'Credit skipped:'), so a future fix to credit rules must be made in two places or the balancing path will diverge from the runtime path.

title: Self-transfer bypasses the allowDeposit lock
detail: findBlockedDeposit is only consulted when source.id !== target.id, so a transfer whose source and target are the same entity can credit a resource marked allowDeposit:false. If any code issues self-targeted transfers, deposit locks are silently ineffective for them.

title: Scanner iterates behavior-rule actions as untyped `any`
detail: action is typed `any`, so action.type/action.value/action.target are unchecked. A schema change to actions (renamed field, non-numeric value shape) would not be caught by the compiler and would silently drop or misclassify behavior levers.

title: initializeWorldState silently no-ops when world blueprint/entity is absent
detail: If the sys_world blueprint lacks components.state, or no sys_world entity exists, the function returns without initializing world state or the worldSeed, so the simulation runs against whatever default state existed with no signal that world configuration was skipped.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: initializeWorldState returns early on a missing world blueprint state or missing world entity without logging; a misconfigured cartridge produces a silently unseeded/unconfigured world rather than an error. Real gap for diagnosing bad cartridges.
